Lock-down at Two Oceans Aquarium

By: Annalise Lubbe | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
With the help of some fancy cameras we walk with the penguins; swim with the sharks and feed the baby turtles during lock-down at the Two Oceans Aquarium.

Unique Selling Point:
More than 500 000 people visit The Two Oceans Aquarium in Cape Town every year. For the first time since opening its doors in 1995, urgent measures have called for a complete lock-down of the aquarium in an effort to prevent the spread of the Covid-19 virus from visitors to the staff. A small team of dedicated staff is on duty, taking shifts to make sure that the thousands of animals in their care are fed and healthy.

Summary:
Since the 20th of March The Two Oceans Aquarium in Cape Town have been on complete lock-down. There are two teams doing alternating day and night shifts. Their top priority? The safety and wellbeing of the more than 10 703 animals in their care.

Some of the animals have been at the aquarium since the opening 30 years ago. Chuck, Farrady and Dorris are African Penguins. They came in as rescues but with the help of dedicated hands, they have settled in well, unlike their cousins along the south-western coast of Africa who have been sliding towards extinction due to overfishing.

Lock-down means there is more time for the penguins to explore and see what the rest of the animals are up to. This morning Jasmin is heading for the shark tank. It is feeding time.

For some of us, self-isolation at home means spending more time with our cats. At the aquarium, it means spending more time with our catsharks! Aquarist, Leigh de Necker takes a hands-on approach. She is making sure that the catsharks and shysharks in her care each get their daily meals.

Many animals in the aquarium will only stay for a while. Sharks are released into the ocean after 5 years. The adult turtles that came in as rescues are nursed back to health, tagged to monitor their movements and then set free to roam the oceans across the world, like Joshi who has swam all the way to Australia on her travels.

This time of the year is a dangerous time for little hatchling turtles as they are picked up in strong currents and end up on the beaches. The aquarium gives them a fighting chance and when they are strong again they are released back into the wild to fend for themselves.


Further information:
Treatment:
With the help of a go pro camera we watch the scenes as they unfold and follow the people as they go around their daily task. We see the penguins on their walk-about through the corridors to the kitchen and the admin offices; we watch the sharks being fed; see the nursing process of baby turtles; follow the food from kitchen to the feed tank and get up close with some of the ocean’s big five. In this rare footage the viewer becomes the observer creating a sense of ‘being there’.

Besides the go pro camera visuals we have archive footage from the Turtle Rescue story shot last year. The style will be observational mixed with some voice over as a guide track. There will be no interviews and no presenter in this three minute insert.

Script:


Script: Lockdown at the aquarium
Duration: 4 minutes
Date: 3 April 2020

V/O The Two Oceans Aquarium in Cape Town is an attraction for thousands of visitors. Here, they can explore the wonderful world of the ocean. It is a space where animals of all sizes can be closely observed...like the ragged-tooth sharks in the big display window, the jellyfish in their colourful tanks, and the penguins as they take their midday nap.

Up music

V/O But on the 20th of March this all changed as the aquarium closed its doors to all visitors. Three days later, the president announced the 21-day National Lockdown. Since then, only a small team of dedicated staff members still look after the more than 10 000 marine creatures in their care - keeping them fed, healthy and active.

Up sound: “Hello, hello, this is little 23. He is getting his little treatment, his wipe-down...very important...get this every day...let’s put it back into the tank.”

Talitha Noble: Conservation Coordinator - Hi, my name is Talitha Noble and I help run the turtle rehabilitation program here at the Two Oceans Aquarium and in this time of lock-down the turtle rehab is running pretty smoothly and to be quite honest quite similarly to the way it normally runs. Self isolation is something we do very well here in quarantine. Our turtles like their own space.

V/O The aquarium is home to many baby turtles that were found stranded on beaches during the winter months, and then nursed back to health in this sanctuary.

Talitha Noble: So it is breakfast time in turtle quarantine. On the menu today we have pilchards.

V/O Pilchards are not only feed to the tiny hatchlings, but are a staple diet for the penguins too.

Ayrton King: Animal Keeper - My name is Ayrton. I am one of the animal keepers at the Two Oceans Aquarium. I have got Grommet with me. Yeh the aquarium is like really carrying on as per normal. It is a lot of changes out in the rest of the world but our routine remains the same. For the sake of our animals to make sure they get all the love and attention they normally get, the food and care as well. And our animals here at the aquarium, they inspire us each and every day and hopefully by sharing a little bit about what we are doing during lock-down with you guys you are inspired as well to just keep going.

Up music

V/O Many of these penguins were rescued and brought into the aquarium and with the help of the dedicated staff, they have settled in well and raised new families.

Up music

V/O Without visitors in the building, the rockhopper penguins take on new adventures, taking a keen interest in what the other animals are getting up to.

Up music

V/O Here, Jellyfish are fed three times a week. Their diet - a seafood mixture that is liquidised to suit their simple digestive systems. Krish Lewis takes care of them.

Krish Lewis: Marine Biologist - Hi there! I am Krish from the Two Oceans Aquarium and even though we are all on lockdown, everything is still very much the same at the aquarium. The jelly still get the five feeds a day. The coral tanks still get fed and looked after so yeah. We have to look after the animals so we have to be here. (with titles)

V/O For every species, feeding time is different. Ragged-tooth sharks are fed only once a week. Their staple diet is hake. The smaller predators, like the catsharks and shysharks are hand-fed three times a week. Here, Leigh de Necker makes sure each gets their fair share.

Up music

V/O The aquarium is a life-support system for many animals and, right now, every member of this critical team is working tirelessly to keep them healthy.

Talitha Noble: Whenever I see these little turtles I am reminded on this time of uncertainty that we must just take it one day at a time. Just keep swimming like the little turtles and take pleasure in little things like a delicious bite of food or being able to stretch our little flippers and so let’s be like turtles and let’s stay positive, yeah.
___________________________________________________________________________
Promo one
The Two Oceans Aquarium has gone very quiet since closing its doors for the national lockdown, but behind these walls, a small team of dedicated staff is still taking care of the animals.

Promo two
Lockdown means more time for the penguins to explore the aquarium and see what the rest of the animals are up to.

Promo three
From baby turtles to penguins and ragged-tooth sharks, how are the sea creatures at Cape Town’s popular Two Oceans Aquarium being taken care of during the National Lockdown?
